title.narrative: Power Up Programme

description.narrative: Power Up! Is a consortium of four women’s right organisations : Just Associates (JASS, lead organisation), Coalition of African Lesbians (CAL), Yayasan Pemberdayaan Perempuan Kepala Keluarga (PEKKA), and Gender at Work (G@W). We will be building, organising, mobilising and transforming power on three strategic agendas, aligned with the Power of women fund’s objectives: 1. Prevention and elimination of sexual and gender-based violence against women and girls – addressed through our bodies agenda. 2. strengthening women’s leadership and women’s participation in (political) decision-making – addressed through our voices agenda.

title.narrative: 5.1. Strengthened and new collaborations with diverse (cross-movement) alliances to support women's leadership and feminist agendas
5.1.1 # of new/diverse alliances created by PU!

comment.narrative: As the indicator measures any new values occurring since the start of the intervention, the baseline value is set at 0. Specific details regarding the situation at the start can be found in the narrative baseline report.
Target is annual, will increase each period

In 2024, Pekka has built a network with 8 local organizations, namely, GOW, IWAPI, PKK, AISYIAH, MSMEs, Village-Owned Enterprises, KTO, and LP2M. Pekka also has built a network with 13 National Organization. In 2024 PEKKA becomes one of the participant in Global AWID network forum.
Target is annual, will increase each period

In October 2021, PEKKA together with 10 WROs with experience in organizing women in micro and small business actors formed the Women's Empowerment for Economic Justice Forum. The ten WROs are; Aisyiyah, ASPPUK, Puspita Bahari Cooperative, FAMM, JASS SEA, KOBETA, Annisa KSU, PERMAMPU, PESADA, and PPSW. This forum aimed to seek support for the development of the role of women in realizing a just economy, and campaign for equitable forms of economic enterprise, including; cooperatives, micro business groups and others.
During 2021, the Forum met thrice and agreed on the name of the network, goals and agenda to be carried out, especially in 2022. Forum members have collected data and information on cooperative members and women micro-enterprises who have been our mantra. These materials will be used as material for the campaign to strengthen women's movements for economic justice. The plan is that the Forum will launch a movement by inviting the government, the business sector, and civil society organizations. In addition, the forum will also campaign for equitable forms of economic business, mass media and social media.
Aside from the national level, PEKKA also initiated economic network meetings in 3 regencies/cities namely; Pemalang - Central Java, Bone - South Sulawesi, and Baubau - South East Sulawesi. The organizations involved include Aisyiyah, Fatayat, GOW (Gabungan Organisasi Wanita or Women's Organization Association) and others.
Target is annual, will increase each period

In collaboration to build joint power, PEKKA joins in an alliance that aims to oversee the implementation of the law on sexual violence crimes. This alliance holds regular meetings to discuss the follow-up agenda after the passing of the law on sexual violence crimes in 2022 to see how far the progress of the implementation of that law has been. This alliance also ensures that there are derivative policies to implement the law on sexual violence crimes down to the grassroots level. we cannot mention of them since it is too many, one of them is KAPAL Perempuan. Not only WROs join the alliance, but also legal aid like LBH APIK.
In 2022, Indonesia hosted the G20 Presidency, where PEKKA participated in voicing its movements at the C20 forum. At the forum, PEKKA explained its role as an NGO in overcoming the economic downturn, especially for women-headed families at the grassroots post-pandemic. In addition, PEKKA also mentioned government policies that tend to be less pro-marginalized groups, so that later it is hoped that the government will be able to make policies that are more inclusive in the future.
At the local-level alliance, the aim of it is to voice the existence of SMEs run by women to the government, from the village to the district level. So the SMEs can be prioritized by the government to access the capital. In 2021, not all PU! areas joined the alliance, so in 2022, the aim of the alliance meeting was only to get to know each other and started to cooperate between organizations. In addition to alliances at the national level, Pekka communities also join in several alliances at local or regional level, such as: - Brebes District; allied with KOBER (stands for Komunitas Brebes Bersama or Brebes Joint Community), where this community focuses on increasing the capacity of each organization. - Mamasa District; allied with AMAN (stands for Aliansi Masyarakat Adat Nusantara or Alliance of Indigenous Peoples of the Archipelago) and LP2M (stands for Lembaga Penelitian dan Pengabdian Masyarakat or Institute for Research and Community Service). - Pacitan District; allied with GOW (stands for Gabungan Organisasi Wanita or Women’s Organization Association) together with IWAPI (stands for Ikatan Wanita Pengusaha Indonesia or Indonesian Women Entrepreneurs Association) and district-level PKK (stands for Pemberdayaan Kesejahteraan Keluarga or Family Welfare Empowerment Organization). - Bolaang Mongondow District; allied with the Forestry Service of Bolaang Mongondow District related to production house assistance to support Pekka Production. - Sijunjung District; allied with GOW (stands for Gabungan Organisasi Wanita or Association of Women's Organizations) on capacity-building activities. - Asahan District; allied with PKBM (stands for Pusat Kegiatan Belajar Masyarakat or Center for Community Learning Activities) UIN Medan, where the Pekka community in Asahan District is taught sewing, making convection to be sold together, facilitated regarding the functions and roles of women. - Bantul District; allied with GOW and Jamu Gendong Organization. - Bima District; allied with IPEMI (stands for Ikatan Pengusaha Muslimah Indonesia or Indonesian Muslim Entrepreneurs Association) where they learn from each other's organisations.
Target is annual, will increase each period

Regarding collaboration and alliances, PEKKA has been involved in a derivative agenda of The Law on Sexual Violence Crimes which was passed in 2021. One of these agendas was PEKKA through the Pekka community in the Power Up! area encouraging City/District Governments to participate in the 16-Day Campaign on Anti-Violence against Women by signing banners as a form of support for efforts to eliminate violence against women (1 signature = 1 support). The signing was carried out simultaneously with FPK (stands for Forum Pemangku Kepentingan or City/District-level Stakeholders Forum) activities involving the City/District Government and their staff.
At the SEA level, PEKKA held a side event at the ASEAN People Forum (APF) with the theme "Women's Group Experiences in Building Economic Independence". This hybrid activity invited 50 people from various NGOs in ASEAN to attend in person and 100 members of the Pekka community to attend online. This side event was aimed at sharing and reflecting on the various experiences of grassroots women in ASEAN countries who formed business groups by applying cooperative principles and trying to create a just economic system. One of The Pekka National Cooperative became one of the speakers sharing the experiences of the Pekka community in growing cooperatives and business groups in an effort to realize a just economic system in Indonesia. This forum was also an opportunity to introduce the Pekka National Cooperative as an economic actor in Indonesia and build a network at the ASEAN level, especially on just economic issues.

title.narrative: 6.1. Increased actions of women using their collective power to demand rights, increase access to resources and ensure collective safety
6.1.1 # of actions by women supported by PU!

comment.narrative: As the indicator measures any new values occurring since the start of the intervention, the baseline value is set at 0. Specific details regarding the situation at the start can be found in the narrative baseline report.

In 2021, PEKKA facilitated the Pekka community to join the BISA KITA (stands for Bisnis Berbasis Komunitas or Community-Based Business) Circular Economy class which focuses on increasing awareness of the healthy and sustainable environment, especially related to 3R (Reduce, Reuse, Recycle), in which there were 3 main activities in the training, such as making soap from used cooking oil, making compost, and processing plastic waste into something worth selling.
In 2022, there were Pekka communities who were still aggressively raising awareness regarding 3R, which are Pemalang District (11 villages) and Mamasa (2 villages). Apart from socializing about 3R, they also teach their community members how to make soap from used cooking oil.
Still related to environmental issues, the Pekka community is also actively developing the Waste Bank. In 2022, the Pekka community managed to organize 19 new Waste Banks in 19 villages in 3 different sub-districts. The Waste Bank is a collective movement to collect non-organic waste at the household level and then the surrounding community can deliver it to the Waste Bank Officer. Furthermore, Pekka Leaders as the manager of the waste bank will sort it out and sell it to other parties to be processed into other useful products that worth selling.
In addition, the Pekka community in East Flores District initiated a tree planting movement which was carried out in the Nelelamadiken Village, where some time ago the village was hit by a flash flood. They also initiated a barter market in Waiwuring Village and the Children's Cultural Festival, where the festival invited children in East Flores District to preserve the weaving culture together.

In 2023, Pekka communities in several Power Up! areas initiated a gardening movement. They planted various kinds of vegetable and fruit plants in the garden, such as kale, spinach, lettuce, chilies, tomatoes, green beans, etc. This gardening movement was managed individually and also in groups. Privately-managed gardens were usually used the home gardens of Pekka community members. Meanwhile, gardens managed as a group used empty land belonging to the village with permission from the Village Government. Regarding the provision of plant seeds and garden management, apart from using self-help funds and grants, the Pekka community advocates for this movement and asks for support from the Village Government. This gardening movement is aimed at ensuring that the prices of vegetables and fruit remain stable and are not affected by market prices. So if the price of raw materials in the market is rising, the Pekka community will not be affected by the price increase. Plants that have entered the harvest period will also only be marketed within the Pekka community because the harvest can only meet the community's needs. In Bima District, West Nusa Tenggara, the Pekka community cultivated azola plants by involving the youth. The society uses these plants for animal feed and as material for making compost.
In 2023, Pekka Communities in several districts/cities established 29 new Waste Banks and continue to manage the existing Waste Banks that have been established before 2023.
Not only the Waste Bank, but since 2021 the Pekka community has started to initiate a waste-free movement. This movement was initiated when they took the BISA KITA (stand for Bisnis Berbasis Komunitas or Community-Based Business) class in 2021 which focused on waste management. The waste they collect is not only sold to the Waste Bank, but is also processed into handicrafts (especially for non-organic waste). In 2023, handicrafts made by Pekka communities began to be exhibited at city/district-level innovation product exhibitions organized by the District Government.
The Pekka Community also initiated the formation of the Forades (stands for Forum Anak Desa or Village Children's Forum), where this forum became the official forum in the village for the youth to voice their interests to the Village Government. Apart from Forades, the Pekka community also activates an art studio for children and teenagers in their village.
In 2024, the local market, which is carried out by PEKKA partners, will receive 6 assistance in the form of places, capital, and equipment for the local market.

In order to build public awareness for environmentally friendly behavior and clean living by managing household waste in order to create a healthy and sustainable environment, PEKKA facilitates their cooperatives and associations in 23 districts/cities to develop various community initiatives. This initiative activity began with Pekka Leaders leading a discussion to discuss problems and seek ideas to solve them. Then they agreed on the initiative activities, made plans and did the division of tasks. After the activity was carried out, the PEKKA Leader would present the learning outcomes of the initiative in a meeting with village leaders and government at the district/city level.
In 2021, Pekka Leaders have initiated: - Bank Sampah (The Waste Bank) in 3 regions. The Waste Bank is a movement to collect non-organic waste in the form of plastic, cans, etc at the household level. Then the household will send the waste to the Waste Bank Officer. Furthermore, Pekka Leaders as the manager of the waste bank will sort it out and sell it to other parties to be processed into other useful products. - Black Bags Movement in 4 regions. Black Bag Movement is a village clean-up movement initiated by Pekka Leaders, name of which refers to the black plastic bags often used to contain domestic waste. In this movement, they invited the society, especially women to pick up the waste around their houses and put them in black plastic bags. After the bag is full, Pekka Leaders will send it to the Pekka Waste Bank (if there is any) or the final waste disposal site.
At the same year, PEKKA held Kelas BISA KITA (refers to Kelas Bisnis Berbasis Komunitas or Community-Based Business Class). It was a series of trainings focused on waste management, such as Used Cooking Oil Management, Collective Compost Processing, and Plastic Waste Management. After the workshop finished, Pekka Leaders mobilize Pekka Community to practice as the implementations of what they got in the trainings. - Used Cooking Oil Management: Pekka Community was taught to process used cooking oil into laundry soap that has both usability and marketability. - Collective Compost Processing: Pekka Community was taught to process organic waste into compost that can be used for farming. - Plastic Waste Management: Pekka Community was taught to process inorganic waste (especially plastic) into useful and economic value goods. The plastic waste is usually processed into shopping bags, pencil cases, pouches, etc.

title.narrative: 6.3. Women's collectives/ groups create feminist economic alternatives
6.3.1 # of economic initiatives developed by women's collectives/groups as a result of PU! interventions

comment.narrative: As the indicator measures any new values occurring since the start of the intervention, the baseline value is set at 0. Specific details regarding the situation at the start can be found in the narrative baseline report.
Target is annual, will increase each period

In 2023, there was no formation of new Pekka Simpin (saving and loans units), but instead focused on the development and sustainability of the Pekka Simpin that had been built previously. Regarding Pekka Mart (grocery store units) and Pekka Production (production units), 16 new Pekka Marts and 111 new Pekka Production were formed. By Pekka Production, many products are produced, such as various kinds of processed chips, dish soaps, chili sauces, herbal medicines, eco-bricks from used bottles, etc. Apart from the collective efforts mentioned above, the Pekka community in Lembata Regency, NTT also manages mangrove tourism along with developing mangrove plants as food. The number of Pekka Production and Pekka Mart increased significantly in 2023 because the alumni of the BISA KITA Class of 2023 formed Pekka Production and Pekka Mart groups after attending the class. Several members who did not take part in the BISA KITA Class were also motivated to form a similar group after realizing that the Pekka Savings and Loans, Pekka Production, and Pekka Mart groups which had been established in 2021-2022 had shown success in improving the economy of Pekka members and marginalized communities in the Pekka community.
Target is annual, will increase each period
In 2024, PEKKA partners have conducted 15 local markets located in 6 districts, namely; Tangerang, Karawang, Brebes, Pemalang, Pacitan, and Bima.
Target is annual, will increase each period

In organizing with women-headed families at the grassroots, PEKKA uses a saving and loans approach using the cooperative method to change the mindset from expecting assistance from the government to relying on their own capacity. In 2022, 19 secondary cooperatives, 1 primary cooperative, and 1 national-level cooperative were formed.
Apart from saving and loans, PEKKA is still developing Pekka Mart and Pekka Production in other areas which don’t have one yet. - Pekka Mart (grocery store units); is a wholesale center for the procurement of basic materials and production materials for the Pekka community and also the society who reside around them, as well as selling the products from other Pekka business units, such as Pekka Production. In 2022, 4 new Pekka Marts have been formed in 4 districts; Brebes, Asahan, Bireun, and Ogan Komering Ilir District. - Pekka Production (producing units); is a collective business that produces basic needs, such as food and clothing products using local materials. Last year, PEKKA managed to form 2 new Pekka Productions units in Bone District.
Target is annual, will increase each period

Since 2002, PEKKA has been organizing poor women-headed family through the growth of savings and loan groups using the cooperative method. This method aims to change behavior and way of thinking, from initially expecting help from outside, to relying on one's own abilities. Even though it is slow, collectively, the savings assets of the Pekka community continue to grow and develop into a sustainable alternative source of finance at the village to district/city level. Furthermore, the capital collected in the Pekka Savings and Loans Cooperative (PEKKA-SIMPIN) is managed by the management for the welfare of members by developing business units: - PEKKA-MART (Grocery Store units); Wholesale center for the procurement of basic materials and production materials for members, as well as marketing products from other business units. - PEKKA-PRODUCTION (Producing units); Collective efforts that produce basic needs such as; food, clothing, and boards with local materials that are around them. - Member Retail Business Unit; personal business managed by Pekka members. This business is a PEKKA-MART network to reach a wider range of consumers. - PEKKA-CBT, a Community Based Travel Business Unit (CBT) is a business managed by Pekka with youth groups by developing cultural tourism packages including stories of Pekka's and community's lives.
In order to expand its network, PEKKA started to gather and organize women-headed families and made a group with savings and loans as the main activity. After the group has been created, PEKKA will conduct them to choose the cooperative's administrators, and they will determine the number of deposits. Deposits here are not only in the form of money but also in the form of goods. These goods will then be sold to other parties so that the cash from the sale can be used as their capital for activities.
In addition, PEKKA also provides training for cooperative administrators, one of which is Training of Trainers (ToT) activities, and provides community assistance (such as group meeting activities, discussions related to the economy and civil rights, etc.). After community training and mentoring activities have been carried out by PEKKA to the community, the cooperative administrators can invite the people who meet PEKKA's member requirements to join the Pekka Community, so that the network will get bigger and community activities are also more diverse, not stopping at Savings and Loans Cooperative or PEKKA-SIMPIN.
And in 2021, there are 31 PEKKA-SIMPIN (Savings and Loan Cooperatives), 31 PEKKA-MART (Grocery Store units), and 72 PEKKA-PRODUCTION (Producing units) in 19 districts/cities in 15 provinces in Indonesia.

title.narrative: 5.3. Increased feminist solidarity and urgent action responses
5.3.1 # solidarity/urgent actions supported by PU!

comment.narrative: As the indicator measures any new values occurring since the start of the intervention, the baseline value is set at 0. Specific details regarding the situation at the start can be found in the narrative baseline report.
Target is annual, will increase each period
In 2024, Pekka will conduct an IWD campaign in 20 districts and a 16 Days of Activism Against Gender Violence campaign in 35 districts
Target is annual, will increase each period

PEKKA shared their experiences in cooperative management with an LBTQI organization (they refused to mention the name of the organization). Related to sharing the experience that PEKKA did with an LBTQI organization in Bandung, PEKKA shared their experience in organizing Pekka economic movement using a cooperative approach. The members of the LBTQI organization were interested and inspired to establish saving and loan activity and applied the cooperative principles since most of them run their MSMEs. Other than that, Pekka’s experience in fighting for their existence is related to their lives.
In the context of solidarity action, at the local level, the Pekka community also provides assistance in cases of violence, including cases of domestic violence, sexual violence, and violence against children. The women at the grassroots who are the victims of any violence against women rarely report their cases to the concerned parties. In Indonesia, we have P2TP2A (stands for Pusat Pelayanan Terpadu Pemberdayaan Perempuan dan Anak or Integrated Service Center for Women and Children's Empowerment) or DP3A (stands for Dinas Pemberdayaan Perempuan dan Perlindungan Anak or Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Service) at the district level that is focused on women empowerment and child protection, but they (the victims) mostly have no intention to report it as they see it as a family disgrace. They keep it for the sake of the good name of their family. They also have the perspective that women (wives) must obey men (husbands), no matter how badly their husbands treat them. That’s why when they become victims of violence, they choose to remain silent. The patriarchal values are still internalized within them. If the violence cases stick to the surface, it is mostly because of the people around them (could be their family, neighbors, etc) who report the case to the concerned parties. In PU! areas, if there are any violent cases, they (the people who report the case) choose to report it to the Pekka community rather than to the village government. The Pekka community’s cadres gain more trust from society since they’ve trained to be a community paralegal, so they have the ability to assist the violence against women and children cases. Paralegals of Pekka work voluntarily and are deemed to be financially easing for the victims, as it might cost much to seek legal assistance.
When the Pekka members get a report of violence cases, they will assist and strengthen the victim to continue reporting it to the concerned parties, such as P2TP2A, DP3A, police officers, or even the courts. So the violent perpetrators can be punished accordingly. The Pekka members will assist it until the case is closed, so the victim will never feel alone during the judicial process.
The "16" represents the sharing session related to PEKKA's experience in cooperative management to an LBTQI organization, 8 case assistance in domestic violence, 5 case assistance in violence against children, and 2 case assistance in sexual violence. We count it by case, not by how many women we assisted.
Target is annual, will increase each period

Since its initiation in 2012, PEKKA and other WROs advocate to goverment and parliament to immediately pass the Legal Draft on the Elimination of Criminal Acts of Sexual Violence. This law is very much needed, because PEKKA has received case reports of women, including girls, who have been victims of sexual violence. It is hoped that this law will provide extra protection to victims. PEKKA's involvement includes discussions among WROs and lobbying to the government and parliamentarians at the national level.
Moreover, in December 2021, Pekka Community organizations (WRO) in 24 regencies/cities were also involved in the Istighosah Akbar (joint prayer) activity to support the ratification of the Sexual Violence Bill which is being discussed in the House of Representatives. The event was attended by 575 people and involved community leaders including Muslim, Christian and Hindu religious leaders.
Target is annual, will increase each period

Together with JASS SEA, PEKKA held an online discussion discussing strategies to support women's agenda in elections, because at that time, Indonesia was entering the election period.
PEKKA also participated in the activity of the Women's Democracy Forum with the theme "Urging the President to Stop the Abuse of Power in Elections". This activity was attended by 54 organizations in Indonesia.
At the local level, the Pekka community is also active in assisting victims of violence against women, for example in cases of domestic violence. Assistance was implemented through litigation (Pekka mediated cases) and non-litigation (Pekka accompanied the victim in filing a divorce lawsuit in court).

title.narrative: 4.2. Enhanced capacity of WROs to design and implement effective strategies and articulate collective political agendas
4.2.1. # of WROs' (political and technical capacities) strengthened by PU!

comment.narrative: As the indicator measures any new values occurring since the start of the intervention, the baseline value is set at 0. Specific details regarding the situation at the start can be found in the narrative baseline report.
Target is annual, will increase each period

In 2023, PEKKA focused on strengthening the organizations that have been strengthened in 2021 and 2022, so that based on quantitative data, there will be no new organizations strengthened by PEKKA. PEKKA agenda continues to strengthen the organization regularly (2-3 times a month) through mentoring activities, not only at the district level (Pekka Unions and Cooperatives), but also at the local level (Pekka Groups). These mentoring activities, apart from supervising the implementation of work plans, also provide learning for the community. Materials that were often taught include economic strengthening, savings and loan bookkeeping, feminist knowledge, community organizing, etc.
Apart from that, to further strengthen the movement of organizations supported by PEKKA, PEKKA also held a ToT related to system change involving members and administrators of Pekka community to encourage systemic change in the context of local economic empowerment. In this system change agenda, the Pekka community initiates what system changes it wants to achieve in the next few years, so that what is produced is not only in the form of output, but also sustainable outcomes. The Pekka community also involves various stakeholders who are each interested in making this agenda a success. This system change agenda will be continued and the progress will be seen in 2024 in the form of joint action with local village governments to create a local economic ecosystem.
In 2023, PEKKA finished developing the Cooperative Website which was initiated back in 2021. This is a website-based platform used to record transactions for Savings and Loans Cooperatives, Pekka Mart, Pekka Production, and Pekka Community Based-Travel. The benefit of this website is to ease the administrators to register members, record transactions, and present financial reports. Through this website, PEKKA transforms the bookkeeping from manual bookkeeping into digital bookkeeping. This eases the administrators to manage, analyze transaction data, and develop the business. Still in the same year, the cooperatives in several districts (Bantul, Karawang, Brebes, Kubu Raya, West Lombok, East Lombok, Lembata, East Flores, Ogan Komering Ilir, Tangerang, Hulu Sungai Utara Districts) received training in using the Cooperative Website.
Target is annual, will increase each period

In 2024, there are as many as 32 cooperatives that have made improvements to the cooperative web stage. There are 11 cooperatives that have used the web and 160 cadres who are involved in cooperative web training. The purpose of this cooperative web training is to train and supervise the process of making cooperative financial statements.
Target is annual, will increase each period

PEKKA has increased the capacity of Pekka cooperatives (especially for 19 secondary cooperatives) and Pekka associations (23 associations in total) in organizing their organizations. The 19 cooperatives were already reported last year, so this year we will report the 23 associations. Apart from encouraging them to voice their opinions more to the village and district governments, the training that is often given is related to activity and financial reporting, so that they can be more accountable in carrying out their activities.
In addition, PEKKA also organizes networking forums that focus on grassroots economic issues named FEMILA. In this forum, there are no administrators, but there is a forum advisor. Their routine agenda is every time there is an event about women in Indonesia, they are obliged to voice their activities and policies on economic justice which so far have not been pro-women and the marginalized.
the number 24 comes from 23 Pekka associations and 1 forum named FEMILA.
Here are some significant results from capacity development: - Cooperative administrators begin to show their leadership qualities, for example being able to make decisions. - The increment of cooperative administrators’ accountability. It is seen in how they wrote their annual cooperative report. After the PEKKA’s finance team checked it, most of them were balanced. For the cooperatives of which the report hasn’t been balanced yet, they can fix it by checking every transaction they made and they can do it themselves without any assistance from the PEKKA team. - Pekka Associations at the regional level are able to conduct advocacy for economic development activities. Some of them succeeded and some of them didn’t, we can see it through those who could access the resources from the stakeholders in the form of funding, goods, training, etc. Usually, the advocacy that hasn’t succeeded yet was caused by the government from the village until the regional level has not responded well to the existence of the Pekka community.
Target is annual, will increase each period

Through training and mentoring, PEKKA has trained Pekka Cooperatives and Pekka Associations (WROs) in managing their organizations, building networks and advocating to the government. In managing the organization, PEKKA trains those administrators to make financial and narrative reports on a regular basis, and every year they must report the progress of their activities to members and stakeholders at the local level through the Annual Membership Meeting.
In addition, PEKKA also trains and assists the management of Pekka Cooperatives and Pekka Associations (WROs) to attend official meetings in villages and districts. They also invited stakeholders to be actively involved in the Village Discussions and Stakeholders Forums they held. In the meeting, Pekka Leaders will share their experiences and lessons learned in developing cooperatives and the challenges they face as well as submit proposals to the government for economic justice. PEKKA's way of advocating has been appreciated by the governments at the village and district levels.

title.narrative: 4.1 Increased leadership capacity and organising skills of women to bring about change in their lives and communities
4.1.1b # women (non-youth) who report increased confidence, political skills and consciousness as a result of PU! interventions

comment.narrative: As the indicator measures any new values occurring since the start of the intervention, the baseline value is set at 0. Specific details regarding the situation at the start can be found in the narrative baseline report.

Activities to increase the capacity and leadership of Pekka communities are regularly carried out from local to national levels. The three mainstay activities held by PEKKA to achieve this goal are the BISA KITA (stands for Bisnis Berbasis Komunitas or Community-Based Business) class, the Akademi Paradigta Class, and the ToT aimed at prospective Akademi Paradigta class mentors.
Two BISA KITA classes were held in 2023, namely the BISA KITA SIMPIN (stands for Bisnis Berbasis Komunitas Simpan Pinjam or Saving and Loans Community-Based Business) and BISA KITA PRODUKSI (stands for Bisnis Berbasis Komunitas Produksi or Production Community-Based Business) classes. For the BISA KITA SIMPIN class, PEKKA already reported it in last year's report because the class started in 2022 and only just finished in 2023, so the quantitative data listed in the actual result value column was only taken from the BISA KITA PRODUKSI class. The BISA KITA PRODUKSI class focuses on increasing knowledge and skills in local resource management, with planning and development of Pekka Production as the ultimate goal. Not only learning theory, the Pekka community was also encouraged to practice what they had learned in class. The output of the BISA KITA class is the establishment of business groups that produce local resources and ultimately improve the economy of Pekka members and marginalized communities in Pekka communities.
The Akademi Paradigta class is a thematic class with a different focus and goal, where 2 types of thematic classes were held in 2023, namely the Akademi Paradigta Change-maker and Entrepreneurship classes. Both classes were held in 30 districts in Indonesia (each class was held in 15 districts). Before holding classes, PEKKA usually organized ToT activities to prepare potential mentors before facilitating academics/mentees in class. The output of the Akademi Paradigta Change-maker Class is the establishment of initiators/activators and change-makers in the community who can promote environmental awareness. The output of the Akademi Paradigta Entrepreneurship Class is the emergence of an economic driver. From these two classes, women emerged as initiators/activators and leaders of change at the community level in environmental, political, social, and economic issues. Class alumni are also involved in public forums, some of them even succeed in holding public positions at the local level.
In 2023, several members of the Pekka community were recorded as taking roles on the public agenda, including: Lembata District, East Nusa Tenggara - One of the heads of the Pekka group in Muruona Village, Ile Ape Sub-district was elected as Village-level PKK (stands for Pemberdayaan Kesejahteraan Keluarga or Family Welfare Empowerment) Secretary Bolaang Mongondow District, North Sulawesi - Sartika Daeng Masenge became Head of Solimandungan 1 Village, Bolaang Sub-district - Ratna Makalalag becomes Head of Hamlet 02, Solimandungan 1 Village, Bolaang Sub-district - Fira Tunggali became Head of Hamlet 01, Solimandungan 1 Village, Bolaang Sub-district - Sulastri Djafar becomes Treasurer of Maelang Village, Sangtombolang Sub-district - Mariyam Paputungan becomes Chair of the Babo Village BPD (stands for Badan Permusyawaratan Desa or Village Council), Songtombolang Sub-district - Loviana Mustaki becomes Head of Hamlet 4, Ayong Village, Songtombolang Sub-district - Ramlah Mokodompit becomes Head of Hamlet 6, Lolak Village, Lolak Sub-district - Amusa Damogalad becomes Head of RT (stands for Rukun Tetangga or Neighbourhood Association) 13, Lolak Village, Lolak Sub-district - Puspawati Ismail becomes Head of RT (stands for Rukun Tetangga or Neighbourhood Association) 01, Lolak Village, Lolak Sub-district - Nirma Pontoh becomes Chair of RT (stands for Rukun Tetangga or Neighbourhood Association) 14, Lolak Village, Lolak Sub-district - Fitri Manoso becomes Secretary of Ambang 2 Village, Bolaang Sub-district
Target is annual, will increase each period

Capacity building is carried out at the national, district/city level, and also at the local level. At the national level, Pekka Community participated in a webinar held to commemorate International Women's Day. In this event, the Minister of Cooperatives also gave a keynote speech and appreciated PEKKA for encouraging the economic movement through the formation of cooperatives in various parts of Indonesia.
In addition, there is also Kelas BISA KITA (refers to Kelas Bisnis Berbasis Komunitas or Community-Based Business Class), where PEKKA provides training to the Pekka Community on how to process organic waste and household waste into compost, make soap from used cooking oil, and process inorganic waste into products with economic value. This activity was attended by 139 people from 23 districts.
At the district/city level, capacity building was carried out intensively in 32 districts in 17 provinces. The training method at the district/city level used the training for trainer method where the potential Pekka Leaders trained in class. Then on the second day, they practiced to lead discussions in groups. On the third day, Pekka Leaders gathered in class again to reflect on the results of the practice, including taking important lessons.
There is also capacity building at the district/city level carried out by the Paradigta Academy (Classes of "Women Lead Everyone A Changemaker"), which aims to develop women's leadership in families, communities and rural communities to become reformers and bring forth the young generation of reformers. The education method is carried out by holding classes which are attended by highly potential village women with a number of participants between 20-35 people per class. Classes are held 2 - 4 times a week for 4-5 hours/meeting. In addition to discussing materials in class, discussion assignments at the family level, discussions with other families, young people, and discussions and action plans with village communities are also given. Another method is to create a WhatsApp group consisting of an Education Coordinator, mentor and participants as a forum for deepening material and discussing other things. A total of 648 participants came from 7 provinces and 15 districts. A total of 340 participants took classes that were fully funded by the Power Up program and 308 people attended classes whose implementation was funded partially by Power Up! and the local government, especially Kubu Raya Regency, West Kalimantan.
Then at the local level, throughout 2021, Pekka Leaders have facilitated group discussions in 71 villages, 33 sub-districts, 11 districts which were attended by 1,559 women. Topics of group discussion include; the importance of saving, forms of saving, the policy of the Village Minister on the use of village funds for women's empowerment, circular economy, local economic movements, and others.
Target is annual, will increase each period

In 2024, APK classes have been held in 20 districts with academics who have passed as many as 537 people. The Cange Maker Class has been held in 15 districts with the number of academics who have passed as many as 445 people. The implementation of the Fair Economy Class this year was held in 23 districts with a total of 6707 beneficiaries.
Target is annual, will increase each period

Regarding leadership and organizational capacity building, PEKKA conducted various trainings held at local to national levels. At the national level, there is the BISA KITA SIMPIN (stands for Bisnis Berbasis Komunitas Simpan Pinjam or Saving and Loans Community-Based Business) class which focuses on savings and loans, in which 200 participants are members of primary, secondary, or national-level cooperatives. The BISA KITA SIMPIN class teaches about 2 significant chapters, which are financial management (transaction flow of savings recap, loan recap, bank cash, and cash books) and cooperative financial reports (profit and loss, balance sheet, distribution of SHU (stands for Sisa Hasil Usaha or Operating Remaining Results). The class not only explains the theory but also invites Pekka community members to practice at the end of each sub-chapter so that participants can directly apply the knowledge they have learned in class. After the graduation, the participants of the class or academies will form an alumna forum, so they are still united in a community. Their activities after graduation are still running, they continue their activities that they have done in the village and also start to organize the society. For the mentor, they will hold a new class with different participants or academies, so that there will be an increasement of the number of the empowered women at the village.
After they (participants of the class or academies) finished their class and graduated, they started to implement the knowledge they got. In the family level, they implemented the value of the role distribution between men and women, relations between men and women in the family, and solving problems within the family. In the community level, they became more empathetic to others, so they felt like they urged to help the society in accessing the health service, social protection, and legal identity. They also organized the society to do initiative activities, such as cleaning the village, establishing a community small business, and initiating the waste bank activity. Furthermore, in order to sharpening their leadership skill, they’re involved in village institutions and are involved in decision making.
In addition, PEKKA also organized Paradigta Academy classes for Change-maker and Entrepreneurship classes. Where before the class was held, PEKKA trained the mentor candidates through ToT (Training of Trainers). Each district in PU! area sent 3 representatives who will later become mentors. After that, the trained mentors can conduct classes in their respective areas (at the local level). Changemaker Class - ToT participants: 15 education coordinators and 45 mentors from 15 districts in PU! areas - Classes were held in 15 districts with 477 academies that successfully graduated Entrepreneurship Class - ToT participants: 15 education coordinators and 15 mentors from 5 districts in PU! areas - Classes are held in 5 districts and are currently still ongoing with 137 academies in total.

In 2024, there are 10 people who are participating in TOT Mentor APK to replace previous mentors who are inactive or fill mentor vacancies. There were 87 participants who took part in the TOT Mentor for the Fair Economy, with the aim of strengthening the capacity of women, marginalized groups to have the ability to manage businesses to encourage the development of the local market, so that they can contribute to efforts to ensure more prosperous communities through a just economy approach. There are 1026 women participated in the Fair Economy Classes.
Target is annual, will increase each period

The implementation of the Akademi Paradigta Changemaker class involves teenagers (aged 9-16 years), both boys and girls (the quantitative data we present only counts the involvement of teenage girls). Their involvement is not as academics/mentees, but as non-government parties who can be invited to work together to jointly develop the village (collaborators).
Their activities were not only limited to discussing books and watching videos in class but also discussed further what activities they would contribute to the development of their village. Their activities focus on literacy and environmental aspects, including: - Build a library in the village. If there was previously a library in their village but it was not active, they initiated the reactivation of the library; - Mobilize the community in the village clean movement and mangrove tree cultivation; and - Initiate and manage the village waste bank.
Target is annual, will increase each period

The youth (mostly teenagers, 13-19 years old) involved in the Paradigta Academy Change-maker class were initially invited to have a class discussion on one of the materials from the module. They then planned together what activities they could do for their village and implemented the plan. These activities included cleaning up the environment in their village and building a reading corner. Apart from having their own activities, they were also involved in activities organized by other communities in their village. The other community activities that they were invited into was related to cultural preservation. For an example in East Flores Regency, they (the youth change-maker) are united in a forum named Village Children’s Forum. There, they learn about their own culture, such as traditional dancing, singing, and weaving. Related to weaving, weaving activities are quite rarely done by the youth, simply because they are not interested. Worried about the loss of this weaving culture, the Village Children’s Forum in East Flores Regency intensified the weaving activities using natural dyes.
Other than that, they were also involved themselves in the socialization of the Law of Child Protection and in the Posyandu Remaja (stands for Pos Pelayanan Terpadu Remaja or center for health care and information for the youth), where they learn and conduct discussion related to the issues they need to have better understanding at, such as recycling organic waste into compost and liquid fertilizer.
By having discussion in one of the materials at Change-maker class, most of them were motivated to actively take roles in the activities at the village. They did it voluntarily without anyone asked them to do so. The discussion was awaken and broaden their perspective that they could also do something for their village.
Target is annual, will increase each period

PEKKA has facilitated Pekka Cooperatives and Pekka Associations (WRO) for advocacy activities to the government to provide support for strengthening the local economy through budgets and policies. The advocacy process is carried out through village-level discussions called “Diskusi Kampung” and district-level discussions called “Forum Pemangku Kepentingan” or Stakeholders Forum. The two discussions were formal meetings initiated by PEKKA to discuss various potentials and challenges in strengthening the local economy.
Throughout 2021, PEKKA has organized 26 Stakeholder Forums in 21 districts/cities in 16 provinces attended by 899 people of which 75.2% are women, including the Pekka Community. Pekka Leaders in 23 districts have also held 62 Village Discussions in 61 villages attended by 1,538 people, of which 72.2% are women, including from the Pekka Community. Participants outside the Pekka community are; village government and community leaders, including women and religious leaders. During the meeting, all local governments expressed their support for Pekka activities in strengthening the local economy in the form of programs and other assistance.
The midline target is set at 50% of the endline target.
